title: Share a creature between browsers, so siblings can trade
description: Rosters live in one browser's localStorage. Clark makes a creature on the tablet and Howie cannot see it — which is the single biggest experiential gap in the Creature Studio. Export one creature (or a whole roster) as a small file or URL fragment and import it elsewhere, re-validated on arrival against the target game. Distinct from llm-rpg-v4i.7, which exports a patch for the REPO; this is kid to kid.

title: Overlays: name the pattern the framework keeps rediscovering
description: This repo has now built the same idea three times without naming it: applyLanguage (same game, other words), applyRoster (same game, extra creatures), and save snapshots (same game, one player's state). All three are 'the shipped game is immutable; everything personal is an overlay, applied at load, never merged into the base'. That is the framework's actual thesis and the reason three different authors — a designer, an LLM, and a child — can work on one world without corrupting each other. Making it first-class makes the next overlay free and makes sharing possible.

title: Autoplayer that can actually finish a game
description: A policy strong enough to complete Emberwood unaided: BFS pathing to waypoints that avoids stepping on portals unless targeted, a combat policy that picks moves by power x type effectiveness x accuracy, heals when low, switches on faint, and grinds wild tiles until a level target is met. A working prototype of all of this was written ad hoc while deriving the Underhearth route (it beat Tace, evolved a starter to Lv28 and reached the boss chamber) — start from that rather than from scratch. Related but narrower: llm-rpg-aiw.18.

title: Derived verification: stop hand-tuning golden scripts
description: The 1251-action Emberwood script is the project's safety net and its ball and chain. It cannot be regenerated — runExplorer stalls at 717 steps and never reaches the summit — so any content change on the walked route is effectively forbidden, and new wild kindred have to be tucked into patches the route never crosses. The fix is not a better script, it is an autoplayer strong enough that golden scripts are DERIVED rather than authored. That turns the pin from a constraint into a product.

title: Web: sprite recolor (palette shift)
description: New apps/web/src/render/recolor.ts. Pure function taking a 104x80 RGBA battler and a hue/palette transform, returning a new one that is still spec-legal: <=8 opaque colours, binary alpha, unchanged silhouette and bounding box. This is what makes a pack battler feel like the child's own with zero art skill. No DOM dependency beyond ImageData so it is unit-testable. Reference the rules in tools/sprite-gen/pixelize.py (--verify) for what spec-legal means.
close_reason: Palette-shift recolor + 9 tests. Invariants independently re-verified on real art (Woxeley: 8 colours in/out, alpha mask identical, binary alpha preserved). Also wired apps/web into npm test, which had no runner.

title: Engine: applyRoster overlay + RosterSchema
description: New packages/engine/src/roster.ts. Pure function applyRoster(game, roster) -> { game, errors } that deep-clones the game and appends studio-made species (and their encounter entries) without mutating the source — same discipline as applyLanguage in language.ts, which is the reference implementation to copy. Zod RosterSchema for the document. Enforces the balance rules: fixed stat budget (240 across hp/atk/def/spd), moves must exist in the target game's catalog, ids must not collide with shipped species, catchRate/xpYield derived from budget rather than author-chosen. Result must still pass validateGame. Export from index.ts. Tests in packages/engine/test/roster.test.ts.

title: Objectives: a standing 'what do I do now?' line (set_objective)
description: It is easy to get stuck: the goal in the header never changes, the HUD shows only map and money, and every instruction is transient chatter that scrolls away. Added set_objective {text} — persists in state.objective across turns and saves, '' clears it, re-stating the same text emits no event. The observer prints it under Goal:; the web renderer shows it as a bar inside the stage (so it scales) with a speaker button and key H that reads it aloud on demand, and speaks a changed objective once cutscene/passage/chatter/choice have drained. Authored into all 22 transition points of The Trial of Job by games/trial-of-job/tools/add-objectives.mjs (idempotent), and translated in lang.simple.json.
design: A first-class command rather than a convention on a magically-named string var: 'new game mechanics = new zod-schema'd data'. The read-aloud button matters more than the bar — for a player who cannot read, 'what now?' has to be answerable by ear, repeatedly.
acceptance_criteria: Objective visible and spoken on a phone; survives snapshot round-trip; old snapshots default to null; translatable; all 4 games validate; golden path still reaches victory.
close_reason: Closed

title: Language overlays: one game, many scripts (+ a simple-words Job for a young listener)
description: A five-year-old cannot follow the Trial of Job's prose, but maintaining a second copy of the game would fork 10 maps, 36 entities, 14 triggers and every flag chain. Added engine-level language overlays instead: applyLanguage(game, overlay) replaces only WORDS, keyed by the original English text, with optional {path,value} patches for the rare structural change. games/trial-of-job/lang.simple.json is a retelling for a young listener - short sentences, concrete nouns, one idea per line - generated and coverage-checked by games/trial-of-job/tools/build-lang-simple.mjs. Web app discovers lang.*.json, offers a 'Words:' row on the title screen, applies via ?lang=<code>, re-validates, and honours the overlay's preferred read-aloud voice.
design: Structure must never be duplicated - it is the thing that rots when forked. msgid-style keys survive reordering and only break when the source wording changes, which is exactly when a translation should be revisited. Patches run BEFORE strings so spliced-in content is still translated. HONESTY RULE for the simple script: the full game quotes the World English Bible verbatim with chapter and verse; a paraphrase must never carry a verse citation, so every one becomes 'from the story of Job'.
acceptance_criteria: 377 rules, 0 reachable strings left in English; overlaid game validates with 0 errors and completes to the victory ending in 138 turns; verified in Brave with read-aloud; 9 engine tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Web: local Piper TTS backend for read-aloud (Web Speech is unusable on Linux)
description: Read-aloud shipped on the Web Speech API, which turns out to be unusable on Linux: Chromium-family browsers delegate to speech-dispatcher, and Brave Origin (de-Googled) exposes zero voices and answers speak() with 'synthesis-failed'. Chrome only works via Google's NETWORK voices, which need internet and send every line of game text to Google. Added a local backend: apps/web/tools/piper-server.py loads a Piper neural voice once and serves WAV on localhost; piper-plugin.ts spawns it from the Vite dev server and proxies /__tts. The Narrator probes it at startup and prefers it, falling back to Web Speech. Offline, private, ~130ms for a three-second line with a medium-quality voice, LRU-cached, with rate and voice selectable from the pause panel.
design: Local-first because read-aloud exists so a non-reader can play — 'depends on the browser's goodwill' is not good enough for that. medium-quality voices are ~8x faster to synthesize than high for no audible loss at game volume, which is what makes the latency imperceptible. hasVoice/voiceHint() are deliberately separate from available: 'the API exists' is not 'something can be heard', and the silent-failure state is surfaced on the chip, in the pause panel and on screen.
acceptance_criteria: Verified in Brave Origin (0 Web Speech voices, speak() -> synthesis-failed): read-aloud plays, passages self-turn, choice menu speaks, pause panel shows Read aloud/Voice/Reading speed, zero page errors, no autoplay blocking.
close_reason: Closed

title: Web: read-aloud narration (Web Speech API) so non-readers can play
description: A player who cannot read yet could not play the web game at all: every beat is text. Added src/audio/speech.ts (Narrator) and wired it through the message box, passage pane, choice menu, title screen and ending screen. Toggle with V (Shift+V cycles reading speed), a corner chip, and rows in the pause panel; the setting persists in localStorage and is off by default. Pacing follows the voice rather than a timer, passages turn their own pages, and the choice menu reads its numbered options and re-reads the highlighted one as the caret moves, so a choice is answerable by ear.
design: Hard invariant: a caller waiting on the narrator is ALWAYS released — superseded utterance, engine error, or a watchdog for engines that never fire 'end'. A stranded waiter means msg.busy() is stuck true and the game freezes, which for this feature's user is indistinguishable from a crash. Stage directions are filtered by shouldSpeak, which fails open so new engine events are spoken rather than silently dropped.
acceptance_criteria: Verified in headless Chromium with a deterministic speech stub: title/passages/dialogue spoken, movement silent, passage pane self-turning, choice options read on caret move, no page errors.
close_reason: Closed

title: Trial of Job Act I: rebuild the Land of Uz as a day loop
description: Act I is currently 'walk east, interact 3x at the altar, leave' — 241 words of trigger tell the player what the calamity took. A reader can be told; a player has to have spent turns on it. Rebuild Act I as 3-5 days in Uz with a per-day action budget: walk the estate, sit with a daughter, count the flocks, go to the evening feast, offer at dawn. The budget means you cannot reach everyone before the day ends, so you choose who. What you tend visibly prospers (set_tile greens the field, spawn_entity grows the flock). Then Job 1:13-19 takes it, and every thing the messengers name is a thing the player personally spent an action on. Same scripture, same fixed outcome — it lands as loss instead of exposition.
design: Agency over HOW/WHEN/HOW MUCH, never over WHAT: the story does not branch. The ledger of what you tended is read back by the messengers and again in Act VI (the flocks return; the ten children do not). Depends on turn triggers for the action budget.
acceptance_criteria: Act I plays as 3+ distinct days with a real budget; messenger text names what the player invested in; game.json still validates 0 errors/0 warnings; golden path in README re-verified.
close_reason: Closed

title: Engine: on:"turn" map triggers (per-action tick)
description: Triggers are only enter/step today, so nothing can happen because time passed — only because the player arrived somewhere. That blocks action economies (a day with a budget), ambient life, timed pressure, and any 'the world responds' beat. Add on:"turn" to TriggerSchema: fires once per accepted world action, after that action fully resolves (movement, interaction commands, step/enter triggers), for triggers on the map the player is standing on. Does NOT fire while a choice is pending, while a battle is active, or on a choose action. once defaults true as today; ambient uses once:false. Combined with add_var/set_var and when, this gives authors tick counters and phase-based scheduling with no new commands.
design: Fire point: end of act(), after all other work, exactly once per act — never re-entrant, so a turn trigger that teleports does not cascade. Must be strictly additive: tiles stays invalid for turn (same as enter), demo+emberwood+job validate with 0 errors/0 warnings, and fromSnapshot tolerates old snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: Schema accepts on:'turn'; validateGame rejects tiles on a turn trigger naming the fix; sim fires it once per move/interact and not during battle/pending choice; deterministic replay preserved; tests cover fire-once-per-action, when-gating, once tracking, and no-fire-during-choice.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make the story come to life: game-feel mechanics for narrative games
description: Trial of Job proved the narrative engine can carry a fixed story, but playing it is 69 moves / 30 interacts / 8 choices across 5539 words — the player's only verb is 'receive text'. The story is fixed and should stay fixed; the fix is player agency over HOW/WHEN/HOW MUCH, and making the player invest actions in what the story later takes away. Borrow the engagement engines that make 2D RPGs (Stardew Valley) work: a day container with an action budget, an accumulating ledger you can see on screen, ambient motion, and discovery that rewards attention. Children cover the enabling engine features and the Act I rebuild that proves the loop.
design: Core thesis: the story is fixed, so make the player BUILD the thing the story destroys. Job 1 names what he had; a reader is told, a player must have spent turns on it. Enabling gap: triggers are only enter/step, so there is no per-turn tick — an action economy or ambient life would need every walkable tile listed as a once:false step trigger. on:'turn' is the unlock.
acceptance_criteria: Epic closes when a human playthrough of Act I reports the day loop as engaging, and the mechanics are general (documented in CLAUDE.md, usable by any game, demo+emberwood still validate clean).

title: Engine: interact target ambiguous with multiple adjacent entities (not facing-based, undocumented)
description: Standing at lighthouse (4,2) between the-great-lamp (4,1, north) and warden-maris (4,3, south) in saltmere-light: after a north bump into the lamp ('The Great Lamp is standing there. Try interact'), 'interact' targeted Maris instead. Target selection with 2+ adjacent entities appears to be list-order (or fixed direction order), not last-faced, and no doc states the rule. This cost a scripted playtest its win; workaround was approaching the lamp from a tile where it is the only neighbor. Fix: prefer the entity in the last-moved/bumped direction, or document the deterministic order in README + forge.md so script authors can plan.
notes: Bumped from P2: the Act I day loop (llm-rpg-565.3) gives each day a two-interact budget, so an interact that resolves to the wrong adjacent entity now costs a whole in-game day, not just a turn. Act I entities are placed so every tendable has at least one unambiguous stand tile, but that is a workaround. Facing-based interact would fix it properly.

title: Turn-based battle engine
description: Deterministic battle sim over a catalog: fight/switch/run actions, speed-based turn order (RNG ties), pokemon-style damage formula with STAB + type effectiveness + 0.85-1.0 roll, accuracy checks, PP, fainting, wild + trainer modes. Pure module, no I/O; seeded RNG.
close_reason: battle.ts: deterministic Battle class, all randomness via injected Rng. Damage floor((floor((2L/5+2)*power*atk/max(1,def))/50+2)*stab*typeMult*roll), STAB 1.5, roll U[0.85,1.0], min 1 dmg when typeMult>0. Turn order by stage-modified spd, rng tiebreak. Escape chance clamp(0.5+0.1*(pSpd-eSpd)/max(1,eSpd), 0.1, 0.95) using stage-free spd, wild only. PP decrements; 0-PP move rejected without consuming round; all-PP-exhausted falls back to built-in Flail (normal/20/never misses). Faint -> needsSwitch free switch (no enemy hit); voluntary switch gives enemy a free attack; enemy auto-replaces. Swappable EnemyAi (default random valid move). state fully JSON-serializable with outcome ongoing/player_won/enemy_won/fled. 15 battle tests pass incl determinism, effectiveness ratios, STAB, seeded miss/run, trainer-forbids-run.

title: Creature catalogs: species/moves/type-chart schemas + sample dataset

Sample fixture dataset with ORIGINAL creature names (no Nintendo IP).

Decisions: type chart supports PARTIAL coverage — missing pairs default to 1.0 so only non-neutral matchups need listing; single atk/def pair so physical/special is descriptive; move effects kept minimal as one-stage raise_/lower_ atk/def/spd (raise targets self, lower targets opponent) so status moves do something. Helpers: speciesById, moveById, statsAtLevel (hp=floor(2b*L/100)+L+10, others +5), movesKnownAtLevel (last 4), typeMultiplier. Fixture test/fixtures/catalog.json: 6 types, 13 moves, 8 species incl emberling->pyrewyrm line, mosskrag dual rock/grass, puddlit. 11 catalog tests pass.

title: Design spike: LLM at runtime without losing determinism
description: An LLM in the running game (NPCs answering free text, flavour rewritten for context, in-character hints when stuck, judging a child's spoken answer to a question) is the single biggest experiential upgrade available — especially with Piper read-aloud already shipped, since a pre-reader could then TALK to a character and be understood. It also threatens the property everything else depends on: seed + action list = playthrough. Decide the contract ONCE rather than ad hoc: the model proposes, the engine disposes (state changes only from an author-declared whitelist), and every model output is recorded into the snapshot so replay reads the recording instead of calling the model. Write it down before anyone builds a feature on it.

title: DOM test harness so screens can be tested at all
description: apps/web now runs 80 tests, but every one of them tests pure logic — the Creature Studio shipped without its rendering or key routing ever being exercised, which was called out honestly at merge. Add jsdom (or a headless browser smoke test) so a screen can be opened, driven with keys, and asserted. Highest value first: the studio's save path and the name field's focus handoff. Extends llm-rpg-7s0.1.

title: Persistent flags: let a game remember you across a new game
description: A save is a self-contained snapshot, so a game literally cannot know you have played before. A small persistent store outside the snapshot — flags that survive starting over — unlocks the whole 'the game remembers you' register that Undertale/OneShot/Heartbound trade on, and which a child finds genuinely magic ('you have been here before'). Small: a namespaced store plus a  reader plus a set_persistent command. Design carefully; it is the one thing that deliberately escapes the determinism boundary, so it must be readable in a snapshot for replay.

title: when { species }: gate on what is in your party
description: 'Bring me a water one' is classification practice, and the children already care about the type chart because they designed the creatures in it. Needs a way to ask whether the party contains a species, or a species of a given type. Turns the roster into a key ring.

title: when { item, op, value }: gate on what you are carrying
description: reads flags, vars, money and party size, but not inventory. Adding an item condition unlocks fetch quests, collecting, trading and counting real objects rather than an abstract var — probably the highest value per line of code in the whole schema. Additive; existing games unaffected.

title: Puzzle primitives: playful progress for a static story
description: The engine gates progress on flags today, so every gate is 'beat a trainer' or 'talk to someone'. Three small, additive schema primitives would turn the same data model into a puzzle vocabulary — fetch, collect, classify, push — without any real-time input, which is what would break determinism. Aimed at edutainment: the learning lives in the doing, not in a quiz.

title: My kindred: a screen for looking at what you made
description: There is a Paddock full of a child's creations and no way to look at them — no list, no stats, no 'this is the one I drew'. A dex screen showing every roster creature (art, name, kind, stats, moves, where it lives) and letting one be edited or removed. The making is currently more rewarding than the having, which is backwards.

title: One overlay contract, composable and order-aware
description: Unify applyLanguage and applyRoster behind a shared contract: pure, deep-clones, returns { game, errors, warnings }, never mutates. Then allow composing several — a language overlay AND a roster today, more later — with a defined order and a report of what one overlay hid or contradicted in another. Today main.ts applies them one after another by hand and nothing checks that a roster entry's name survives translation.

title: npm run balance: simulate every fight across level bands
description: A repo tool reporting, per trainer and per level band, the player's win rate over N simulated fights. This was hand-rolled twice in one session — once to tune the Underhearth (it revealed the road trainers won 80-100% and contributed nothing) and once to check catch rates. It should not be scratch work. Output a table the way the reach report does. Related: llm-rpg-85g.16 (multi-seed explore sweep).

title: Web: the studio UI
description: The creation flow: pick a body from the unused pack battlers, recolor, name it, choose a type, spend the stat budget, pick moves. Validates live and refuses to save something validateGame would reject. Touches main.ts and style.css, so it lands after the isolated pieces.
notes: FLOW FINDING from wave 2, verified by cross-validation: a photographed PENCIL sketch imports as a greyscale sprite (correctly — pencil on paper has no colour). So in the studio flow the recolor step is not cosmetic, it is how a hand-drawn creature gets any colour at all. Order the UI as: photograph -> import -> recolor -> name/type/stats/moves. Also expect edge speckle from photo noise on raw phone photos; consider offering the recolor/palette step as a chance to clean up, or a 'tidy edges' toggle. Import of an already-coloured image (AI-coloured or drawn digitally) needs no recolor.

title: Web: roster storage + apply on load
description: Persist the roster document in localStorage next to saves (llmrpg:roster:<gameId>), apply it through applyRoster when the game loads, and hot-swap the running game the way the dev forge does — preserving position, party and battle via snapshot. Reject invalid rosters gently the way saves.ts rejects damaged saves: never throw out of the module.
notes: INTEGRATION FINDING from wave 1, verified: applyRoster attaches spriteDataUrl onto the generated species object, and a validateGame round trip STRIPS it (SpeciesSchema has no such field, and zod drops unknown keys). Do not rely on it surviving. The web app resolves art through the SpriteMap built from games/<id>/sprites.json keyed by species id — not through the species object — so this layer should build a sprite-map overlay from the roster instead, alongside the game overlay. Verified with a round-trip script; applyRoster itself is correct, the field just cannot ride there.

On a Steam Deck the game runs but needs Steam Input mapping a controller to arrow keys; on a phone it loads but cannot be played at all. Add (a) Gamepad API polling in the rAF loop mapping d-pad/stick to movement, A to interact/advance, B to back, Start to pause, and (b) on-screen touch controls (d-pad + action button) shown when a touch device is detected.

title: Simple-words Job is 138 turns, not the ~50-60 a 5-year-old wants
description: The language overlay trimmed the friends from six rounds to three (candor threshold moved 4 -> 2), taking the golden path from 152 to 138 turns. That is far from the one-sitting target: the length is MOVEMENT, not text — 108 of 152 turns on the full path are walking a 16x12 estate and five whirlwind maps. Cutting it further means structural work an overlay should not be doing: shrink or merge maps, cut the number of tendings per day from 2 to 1, or collapse the whirlwind's five maps into one (llm-rpg-565.6 already proposes that for its own reasons). Saves work, so it is playable across sittings in the meantime.
acceptance_criteria: A young player can finish the simple script in one sitting (~50-60 turns), without forking game.json.

title: Act I day loop: movement is still ~70% of inputs
description: The rebuilt golden path is 152 turns: 108 moves, 36 interacts, 8 choices. Movement went from 65% of inputs to 71% — the day loop added real decisions but also a lot of walking across a 16x12 estate whose tendables sit at the corners. It is now walking a route the player chose rather than walking between fixed beats, which is better, but it is still the largest single cost. Candidates: cluster the tendables, shrink the estate, or give the player a way to cover ground (the herd dog as a mount is a joke, but a 'go to' verb or a shorter estate is not).
acceptance_criteria: Move share on the golden path drops below 60% without cutting decisions.
notes: Measure with games/trial-of-job/tools/golden-path.mjs, which regenerates the path by driving the Sim.

title: Ambient motion: the world is never still
description: Nothing on any map moves unless a cutscene explicitly moves it, so every map reads as a diorama. Stardew is never still — that stillness is most of the gap between 'a place' and 'a screen'. With on:'turn' triggers landing, ambient motion is authorable as data: a once:false turn trigger that ticks a var and moves entities on a phase. This bead covers proving that pattern (sheep drifting, a dog that follows, feast-house bustle), finding where it is too painful to author, and adding the minimum sugar needed — candidate: move_entity accepting a wander/toward form, or a way to reset a counter without a second trigger (there is no modulo op in when).
design: Prefer data patterns over new commands. Only add sugar after authoring the Uz estate ambient layer for real and seeing what hurts.
acceptance_criteria: Uz estate has visible ambient life; the authoring pattern is documented; any new schema is strictly additive and demo+emberwood still validate clean.
close_reason: Closed

title: Weekly scripture game pipeline
description: The recurring workflow proven by The Trial of Job: (1) pick the week's text and write docs/design/<story>.md following job.md's fidelity rules (quotation sacred, canonical beats not choices, reverent depiction, WEB translation); (2) launch a worktree-isolated Opus build agent with Forge-only authoring + verified scripture fetching + the six verification gates (validate, forge_check, explore reaches an ending, golden-path script, opening played by hand, suite green); (3) merge, verify independently, close beads. Candidate structures for coming weeks: Ruth (loyalty choices), Jonah (the refusal arc), Esther (courage gates), the Exodus plagues (cutscene showcase). Each build also files friction beads.

title: Reachability: no way to declare an observed-scene map intentionally off-stage
description: The observed-scene pattern (docs/forge.md) builds a map the player never walks — The Trial of Job's heaven-court, focused by camera_focus during two cutscenes. analyzeReachability necessarily reports it as an unreachable map with 3 unreachable entities, so forge_check's verdict is a permanent 'fail' and the game's acceptance gate can never be green without a prose exception. Proposal: a map-level flag (e.g. maps.<id>.offstage: true, or a 'observed' role) that the analyzer counts as intentional — reported, not failed — so authors keep a clean signal. Alternative: verdict 'pass with declared exceptions'.

title: No way to change the player's own appearance mid-game (player variants / set_player_sprite)
description: Entities have variants and set_variant; the player has only player.glyph (setPlayerStart) and sprites.json player. In a first-person narrative game the protagonist IS the player, so a before/after transformation — Job struck with sores from the sole of his foot to his head — cannot be shown on the character the player is looking at. The Trial of Job satisfies its 'afflicted variant' requirement on a proxy NPC (job-seen, the man as the heavenly court sees him) and forces it with set_variant. Proposal: player.variants (same schema, when-evaluated) plus a set_player_variant / set_player_sprite command.

title: CLI replay mode (--actions) never prints the start map's enter-trigger events
description: The start map's 'enter' trigger fires before the first act (its events sit in lastEvents at construction). In interactive mode they are shown; in --actions replay mode the CLI prints per-action events only, so a narrative game's cold open (show_title, opening passage, play_music) is invisible in scripted play. In The Trial of Job the whole Act I title card and Job 1:1–3 never appear in the golden-path transcript. Fix: cli.ts replay mode should flush the pre-first-action events before running the script.

title: Passage citation convention: engine prepends the em dash, so authored '— Job 1:1' renders as '— — Job 1:1'
description: sim.ts formats a passage citation as `— ${cmd.citation}`. docs/design/job.md (and the acceptance brief) show citations written as '— Job 38:4–7, WEB', and apps/web/src/passagetest.ts shows them bare ('Job 38:4–9'). Authoring the dashed form is silent — no validation warning — and every passage in The Trial of Job rendered '— — Job 42:16–17, WEB' until 39 setDialogue/setTriggers ops were re-issued. Fix: validateGame warns when a citation starts with an em/en dash, docs/forge.md field schema states 'citation: bare reference, the renderer adds the dash'.

title: Explorer interaction key ignores vars: add_var-only progress never re-opens an entity
description: autoplay.ts keys interactions as `${entityId}|${flagsKey()}` — flags only. A narrative beat that advances a var (add_var days_of_silence 1) and nothing else is interacted with exactly once by the explorer, so any repeat-interaction mechanic (the seven days of silence, the three offerings, the three mourning acts) is invisible to playtesting unless the author also sets a distinct flag per step. The Trial of Job works around it with silence_1..silence_7 / offering_1..3 / mourn_1..3 flags. Fix: include a vars digest in the dedupe key (or a per-entity interaction-index digest).

title: Narrator voice for entity-sourced text (narrate command or say voice)
description: Entity-sourced 'say' always renders as Name: "text" (sim.ts execCommands). Objects that are places, not speakers — an altar, a mat in the ashes, the dust of a courtyard, a waystone — have no way to narrate. In The Trial of Job this forced 52 uncited 'passage' commands to carry ordinary narration (the passage pane is meant for text that deserves shape). Proposal: a 'narrate' command, or say { voice: "narrator" }, that prints bare from any source, exactly like trigger-sourced say.

title: Web: play lastCues with real pacing, per-variant sprites, ending screens
description: Engine side is done (djt.3-5): state.lastCues carries ordered cutscene records (move_entity/spawn/remove/set_tile/wait/camera_focus/play_music/screen_effect/show_title), entities expose effective sprite ids via variants, and state.ending = {id, text} distinguishes endings. apps/web should: pace cues (walk animations, camera pans incl. other-map observed scenes, title cards, waits in beats, music, shake/flash/fade), map variant sprite ids through the manifest, and show distinct ending screens per ending id (victory keeps the win screen).

title: Forge: rejected batch response renders the discarded draft state (validation OK + map render)
description: When forge_batch rejects (all-or-nothing, 'NOTHING was written'), the response still appends 'validation: OK — the game is fully valid and playable' plus an ASCII render of the touched map — both computed from the rolled-back draft, not the on-disk file. In the 85g.6 run the render showed a fully-built harbor map while games/<dir>/game.json still had zero maps (a following forge_map call errored 'unknown map'). An LLM reading that response can easily conclude the batch half-landed. Fix: after a rejection, report the persisted state (or omit render/validation and say 'state unchanged').
close_reason: runOps in forge-mcp.ts now reports only the PERSISTED document: on rejection it prints the op errors, an explicit 'game.json is unchanged — the state below is the CURRENT on-disk file, not the rejected draft' label, validation of the on-disk doc, and renders from the on-disk doc (a map only the discarded draft had renders as 'unknown map', reinforcing nothing landed). Pinned by a real-MCP-client e2e test (rejected createMap+bad-paint batch).

title: Forge guide: portal workflow contradicts linkPortal (bidirectional to missing map is rejected)
description: docs/forge.md step 3 says 'Link portals as you go (linkPortal, usually bidirectional: true). A portal to a not-yet-created map is a normal draft state' — but linkPortal with bidirectional:true REJECTS when the destination map does not exist ('bidirectional needs map X to exist'). Only one-way dangling links are draft-able. Either fix the guide (link one-way while drafting, add the return link after createMap) or make the op queue the reverse half until the map exists. Found in 85g.6 acceptance run: first map batch died on its final op because of this.
close_reason: Decision: keep linkPortal strict (a bidirectional link writes the return portal, so the destination map must exist — deferred/queued reverse halves would be invisible state). Fixed docs/forge.md step 3 to match: one-way links to missing maps are the draft state; bidirectional works within one batch when createMap precedes it, or re-run linkPortal bidirectional after createMap (portal-per-tile replacement makes it idempotent). Op table row updated too.

title: Whirlwind as a collection space, not a five-map corridor

title: Ash heap as an endurance loop (composure, not HP)

The friends are a relationship ledger running in REVERSE: speaking honestly degrades standing with them, and honesty is what turns out to be right (Job 42:7). Replaces the seven identical ash-seat interacts and the 6 read-then-pick-1-of-3 cycle beats. Depends on turn triggers.

title: No way to hide a var from the observer's Vars: line
description: observe.ts prints every var as a 'Vars: candor=6, prayers=3' line. The Trial of Job's candor axis is designed to be invisible to the player ('conscience is not a meter') — it is hidden in the web renderer but fully exposed to any text-mode player or LLM. Proposal: a naming convention (leading underscore) or a game-level 'hiddenVars' list that observe omits, while keeping them in snapshots and playtest reports.

title: Forge server forgets the active game between connections
description: forge-mcp.ts keeps the active game in process memory. A scripted client (or any session that reconnects) must re-issue forge_open before every batch or every op is rejected with 'no active game'. Authoring The Trial of Job across ~10 driver runs meant prepending forge_open to each. Proposal: persist the active dirName next to the games dir (or default to the single game when only one exists).

title: Non-blocking entities cannot stand on non-walkable tiles
description: validateGame errors on any entity whose position is a non-walkable tile ('position (1,1) is on non-walkable tile "water"'). That is right for interactables, but it blocks purely decorative scenery: Behemoth and Leviathan were meant to lie in the water at the edge of the whirlwind map and had to be beached on the sand. Proposal: allow blocking:false entities on non-walkable tiles (they can still be interacted with from an adjacent walkable tile — or warn instead of erroring when no walkable tile is adjacent).

description: djt.8 added forge ops (setMeta, setTriggers/addTrigger/removeTrigger, setVariants, removeCatalog), playtest report fields (battleDetails[], completed, tail option / --tail), reachability teleports[]/limitations[], explorer step-trigger targeting and exhausted gate diagnosis, and the docs/forge.md narrative chapter. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md architecture summaries predate this; update them (they were outside the djt.8 agent's file ownership). README and docs/forge.md are already current.

title: Overlay-aware planning: explorer/reachability full simulation of runtime overlays
description: Follow-up to llm-rpg-ran (closed with teleport edges + stated limitations). The static analyzer and the explorer's BFS still plan against static maps/entity positions: set_tile walls/openings, spawned blocking entities, remove_entity openings, and move_entity relocations are only documented as limitations (ReachabilityReport.limitations) and caught dynamically by the explorer's stall guard. Full fidelity would mean the explorer planning via sim.entitiesOn/tileAt (overlay-consulting reads) and reachability modeling conditional overlay effects. Decide if the payoff justifies the complexity — the explore playtest already exercises the real sim.
notes: Confirmed while authoring The Trial of Job (llm-rpg-djt.9): the explorer plans interactions from game.maps[*].entities only, so spawn_entity NPCs are never interaction targets and move_entity NPCs are pathed to their pre-move tiles. Practical consequence for narrative authors: any story-critical NPC must be statically placed (reveal it with variants instead of spawning it). Job's three friends and Elihu are placed from the start and appear as 'A Traveler on the Road' / 'A Young Man, Waiting' until their arrival flags flip the variant; only scenery (the four messengers, the restored flocks, the three daughters) is spawned.

title: Autoplay/reachability are overlay-blind: explorer BFS plans against static entity positions and reachability ignores set_tile/teleport_player/spawned blockers
description: runExplorer (packages/play/src/autoplay.ts) and analyzeReachability (reachability.ts) read game.maps statically. Games using djt.3 overlays (moved/spawned/removed entities, set_tile walls, teleport_player edges) can diverge from the plan: the explorer's stall guard catches it but coverage suffers, and reachability can report false unreachables/reachables. Consider consulting sim.entitiesOn/tileAt (explorer) and modeling teleport_player/set_tile edges (reachability).
close_reason: Reachability: teleport_player commands are now BFS edges — harvested from every command list (interactions, rewardCommands, triggers, choice options, spawn payload dialogue) with host + gating, applied to a fixpoint; gated teleports (when/requiresFlag anywhere on the chain; rewardCommands/spawn-payload conservatively gated) fire in the optimistic pass only. Report gained teleports[] and limitations[] — the honest boundary: set_tile/spawn_entity/remove_entity/move_entity overlays are NOT simulated (stated per-game, echoed in forge_check description and README). Explorer: targets unfired once step-trigger tiles (when-gate evaluated live), and narrative success is explicit — reports carry completed = win || ending!=null; CLI exit 0 for catalog-free games on any ending; win keeps its meaning. Residual full overlay-aware planning filed as a follow-up bead.

title: Choice menu polish: distinct refuse SFX on Escape, scroll affordance for >8 options, consider styling the 'You choose: X' chatter beat
description: Follow-ups from llm-rpg-djt.11. (1) Escape on the choice menu shakes+blips; a dedicated 'denied' SFX would read better than the nav blip. (2) .choice-list overflows with overflow-y:auto past ~320px, but there is no visual hint that more options exist below. (3) The engine's 'You choose: <label>' line is kept in chatter deliberately (it is not a mirror duplicate); consider emphasis styling or suppression once real games use choices heavily. (4) Mouse: clicking the message box does not advance chatter while a choice is queued behind it (keyboard advance works); consider a click-to-advance on #msgbox.

title: Passage pane polish: shared passage-event rendering + reading niceties
description: Follow-ups from the djt.7 web half. (1) The web drops the engine's mirrored multi-line passage event from the chatter box by re-rendering each lastPassages entry and exact-matching the string (apps/web/src/ui/overworld.ts withoutPassageEvents). If the engine's formatting in sim.ts case 'passage' ever changes, the filter fails open and the passage text shows twice (pane + chatter). Export the renderer from the engine (or tag passage events) so web and engine share one source of truth. (2) Reading niceties: optional soft page-turn SFX; widow control so a passage's final page doesn't carry a single orphan line; consider dimming the advance marker on the final page of the final passage. (3) Battle-time passages are currently impossible (interactions are overworld-only) — if a future command can emit passages mid-battle, verify pane-over-battle layering and the exit-battle gating in main.ts loop.

title: Decide: empty-valid catalog (loosen typeChart.types/moves/species min(1))
description: djt.6 mentioned 'catalog optional or empty-valid (typeChart currently requires >=1 type — loosen)'. The engine half shipped catalog-as-optional instead; an empty catalog object still fails CatalogSchema (types/moves/species each min(1)). Decide whether {typeChart:{types:[],effectiveness:{}},moves:[],species:[],items:[]} should ALSO validate as a narrative game (forge blank drafts would then validate earlier). If yes: loosen the min(1)s, treat an empty catalog exactly like an absent one in validateGame/Sim, and keep existing games byte-identical.
close_reason: DECISION: optional-only stays; an empty catalog object remains INVALID. Rationale: an empty catalog almost always means an unfinished battle game and validation should keep naming the missing pieces; absence of the key is the explicit narrative signal, so the two states stay distinguishable and existing games stay byte-identical. The ergonomic gap (blank drafts couldn't become catalog-free) is closed by the new removeCatalog op, which refuses while moves/species/items remain so the deletion is deliberate. Documented in docs/forge.md ('Why there is no empty catalog').

title: forge_map: overlay trainer line-of-sight coverage
description: forge_map renders tiles, entities, portals and the encounter table, but a trainer's lineOfSight {dir, range} — the thing that decides whether a route trainer is avoidable — is invisible; in the 85g.6 run the LOS column had to be computed by hand to guarantee the road crossing engages. Suggest marking covered tiles (e.g. '!' or a listed tile range per trainer in the key) so avoidability is visible at a glance.

title: Forge: multi-seed explore sweep for balance tuning (single-level edits perturb the RNG stream)
description: Balance tuning in the 85g.6 run was whack-a-mole: changing one trainer's level reshuffles the deterministic RNG stream, flipping OTHER seeds between win/loss (boss opener 8->7 made seed 1 lose and seed 2 win). Proving robustness meant calling forge_playtest explore 5x with seed 1..5 after every tweak and eyeballing. Wanted: forge_playtest accepting seeds:[...] (or count:N) returning a compact per-seed win/steps/battles table plus aggregate win rate — one call per balance iteration instead of five.

title: Forge: blank template legend lacks ',' road tile named as core vocabulary in the guide
description: forge.md 'Schema conventions' lists the boring shared vocabulary as '# tree/wall, . grass, , road, ~ water, * tall grass' — but the blank template's legend ships only '. # ~ *'. Every blank-start author must addTile ',' themselves before painting the first road (85g.6 run did). Add ',' to the blank template legend (and consider '=' floor / '%' wall too, since the guide recommends them for interiors).
close_reason: Blank draft legend (createGame) now ships ',' road (🟨), completing the guide's core vocabulary . # , ~ *; starter template gained '~' water for full parity (guide updated to say both templates ship all five). Interior chars = and % stay addTile-on-demand per the guide's own advice.

title: Explore report: stopDetail should name the undefeated gate trainer / unmet flag blocking progress
description: When the explorer loses a trainer battle it never re-challenges (see llm-rpg-aiw.18 for the policy fix), and the run ends stopReason=exhausted with stopDetail 'no reachable pending targets left (every reachable entity interacted with in the current flag-state...)'. That wording hides the actual blocker: in the 85g.6 run the real story was 'lost to net-mender-oda; oda_defeated gates knotted-bar which gates the lighthouse'. The static check already knows the flag->gate graph; the explore report should say which lost/unfought trainers set flags that pessimistically gate unreached content.
close_reason: Explorer 'exhausted' stopDetail now appends a gate diagnosis: trainers it lost to TRAINER_LOSS_CAP times and gave up on (naming the unearned defeatFlag) and still-closed passableWithFlag gate entities (naming the needed flag). Tested with a doorwarden fixture; wording pinned.

title: Forge docs: catalog/entity field schemas missing from forge.md; README species example omits required 'types'
description: forge.md's op table names args ('species', 'move', 'item', 'entity', 'tile') without listing their fields, and README's 'Game format in 30 seconds' species example has no types field at all — but addSpecies requires species.types (array). First addSpecies attempt in the 85g.6 run was rejected ('species.types: Required; Unrecognized key type'). Rejection messages do name the fix (good), but the authoring guide should carry a minimal field list per object (species: id, name, types[], glyph, baseStats{hp,atk,def,spd}, learnset, catchRate, xpYield, evolvesTo?; move: id, name, type, power, accuracy, pp, effect?; item: id, name, kind, amount|ballMod; tile: name, glyph, walkable, wild?), and the README example should include types.
close_reason: docs/forge.md gained a 'Field schemas' chapter (tile/species/move/item/entity/interaction/trainer/trigger/variant/command minimal field lists); README's 30-seconds example species now carries name/glyph/types and the move carries name — both copy-paste-valid against the real schemas.

title: Forge polish: web hot-reload follow-ups
description:

The edit layer covers createMap + painting but consciously skipped map lifecycle: removeMap (only if unreferenced by portals/player.map/player.respawn, or with a cascade option), renameMap (rewrite portal toMap refs, player.map, respawn.map), and resizeMap (grow/crop rows with a fill char, rejecting crops that would orphan entities/portals). title: Playtest: smarter battler policy for goal mode
description: The explorer's greedy battler (highest-power usable move, no items, no catching, no grinding) loses to tuned trainers (Emberwood explore run: 1 won / 10 lost, stuck at badge_fern). Improvements: type-effectiveness- and accuracy-aware move scoring, heal items in battle, optional catch-to-fill-party, and a grind loop that levels on wild tiles before re-challenging a trainer after a loss. Keep it deterministic (no Math.random).

Emberwood works around it by inlining Vespera's defeat line as the first rewardCommands say and omitting defeatText. Consider emitting defeatText before rewardCommands.
